mainTopic: Identifying prophets through their names, אגדות about famous women, and דרשות on מגילת אסתר chapters 4–5
overview: The גמרא continues its list of prophets descended from רחב and asks how we know their fathers were prophets too. עולא answers that a father named in a prophetic verse was also a prophet, and a ברייתא adds that ancestors named with praise or blame share in it. רב נחמן's claim that מלאכי is מרדכי is refuted by a ברייתא that lists them separately. רב נחמן then supports the view of רבי יהושע בן קרחה that מלאכי is עזרא, since both fought intermarriage. Next come ברייתות about famous beautiful women, including the power of רחב's name. The גמרא then returns to explaining פסוקים in מגילת אסתר: מרדכי's cry, אסתר's fright, התך as דניאל, אסתר going to the king willingly, and her being clothed in רוח הקודש. A string of teachings from רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי חנינא follows: on the blessing and curse of a הדיוט, on quoting in the name of the speaker, and on the loss of a צדיק. The amud ends as רב חסדא begins to explain why seeing מרדכי made המן feel his success was worthless, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How do we know the fathers were prophets?
steps.stepSummary: The sons in the list of רחב's prophetic descendants are clearly prophets, but where do we learn that their fathers were prophets too?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, regarding them (the sons), it is stated explicitly. But their fathers, from where do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is looking back at the eight prophets said to come from רחב. It accepts that the four sons are clearly prophets, but asks for a source that the four fathers were prophets too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירמיהו, ברוך, חנמאל and שריה are each shown as prophets by the verses themselves. Their fathers (חלקיה, נריה, שלום, מחסיה) are never directly called prophets. So the גמרא needs a rule that turns a father's name into evidence that he was a prophet.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (accepts one part before asking about another)
They are stated explicitly
Their fathers
From where do we know?

phrases.english: Granted, regarding them, it is explicit,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the four sons; the verses say outright that they were prophets.

phrases.english: but their fathers, from where do we derive it?
phrases.notes: The fathers are never directly called prophets in the verses.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא אִינְהוּ מִיפָּרְשִׁי, אֶלָּא אֲבָהָתַיְיהוּ מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier list (earlier) of eight prophets descended from רחב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the fathers of the listed prophets were also prophets.

steps.title: עולא's rule about names in prophecy
steps.stepSummary: עולא teaches that when a prophet is named together with his father, the father was also a prophet. When a prophet is named with his city, he came from that city. When no city is given, he came from ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like עולא, for עולא said: Wherever a person's name and his father's name appear in a context of prophecy, we know he was a prophet the son of a prophet. If his name appears without his father's name, he was a prophet but not the son of a prophet. If his name and his city are stated, he was from that city. If his name appears without his city, he was from ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a rule from עולא: a father's name in a prophetic introduction tells us the father was a prophet too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule treats every detail in a prophet's introduction as meaningful. Naming the father means the father was also a prophet, and leaving him out means he was not. The same logic applies to the city: if no city is named, the default is ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: Prophecy
It is known / we can be sure
A prophet, the son of a prophet
His city

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule fills the gap from step 1. The fathers of the four prophets are named in the prophetic verses, so they too were prophets.

phrases.english: As Ulla taught.
For Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשְּׁמוֹ וְשֵׁם אָבִיו בִּנְבִיאוּת —
phrases.english: Wherever his name and his father's name appear in prophecy,
it is known that he is a prophet, son of a prophet.
His name but not his father's name:

phrases.aramaic: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁהוּא נָבִיא וְלֹא בֶּן נָבִיא,
phrases.english: it is known he is a prophet, not son of a prophet.
His name and his city's name stated:
it is known he is from that city,
His name but not his city's name:
it is known he is from Jerusalem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Naming the father in a prophetic introduction shows that the father was also a prophet.

steps.title: A ברייתא on righteous and wicked lineage
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches a similar rule. When the verse mentions a person with his ancestors in a praiseworthy way, both he and his father were righteous. When it does so in a negative way, both were wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: Anyone whose deeds and whose ancestors' deeds are not described, and the verse mentions one of them favorably, like 'The word of ה׳ that came to צפניה son of כושי son of גדליה,' we know he was a righteous man, son of a righteous man. And whenever the verse mentions one of them unfavorably, like 'In the seventh month ישמעאל son of נתניה son of אלישמע came,' we know he was a wicked man, son of a wicked man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a parallel rule. Listing a person with his ancestors tells us about the ancestors' character, not only their identity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This takes עולא's idea a step further. Listing ancestors is not just a family tree. If the context is praise (a prophecy to צפניה), the ancestors share in the praise. If the context is negative (ישמעאל, who murdered גדליה), the ancestors share in the blame.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Unstated / not described
In praise / favorably
Unfavorably / in disgrace
A righteous man, son of a righteous man
A wicked man, son of a wicked man

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Anyone whose deeds and his ancestors' deeds are obscure,

phrases.aramaic: וּפָרַט לְךָ הַכָּתוּב בְּאֶחָד מֵהֶן לְשֶׁבַח,
phrases.english: and the verse specified one of them favorably,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן: ״דְּבַר ה׳ אֲשֶׁר הָיָה אֶל צְפַנְיָה
phrases.english: for example: "The word of the Lord that came to Zephaniah
phrases.notes: צפניה 1:1

phrases.english: son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah":
it is known he is a righteous man, son of a righteous man.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁפָּרַט לְךָ הַכָּתוּב בְּאֶחָד מֵהֶן לִגְנַאי,
phrases.english: And whenever the verse specified one of them unfavorably,
for example: "And it was in the seventh month
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 41:1

phrases.aramaic: בָּא יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֶּן נְתַנְיָה בֶּן אֱלִישָׁמָע״ —
phrases.english: Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama came":
phrases.notes: ישמעאל killed גדליה בן אחיקם.

phrases.english: it is known he is a wicked man, son of a wicked man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel ברייתא that extends עולא's rule from prophecy to righteousness and wickedness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ancestors named in a favorable verse were righteous, and ancestors named in an unfavorable verse were wicked.

steps.title: רב נחמן: מלאכי is מרדכי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the prophet מלאכי is really מרדכי. He was called מלאכי because he was second to the king (מלך).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: מלאכי is מרדכי. Why was he called מלאכי? Because he was second to the king.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new claim from רב נחמן that the prophet מלאכי and מרדכי are the same person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן reads the name מלאכי as built on the word מלך (king). It hints at מרדכי's role as second to King אחשורוש, as described at the end of the מגילה.

keyTerms.meaning: מלאכי, the last of the prophets
Second to the king

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Malachi is Mordechai,
and why was he called Malachi?
Because he was second to the king.
phrases.notes: A wordplay: מלאכי sounds like מלך.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מַלְאָכִי זֶה מָרְדֳּכַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about identifying prophets.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מלאכי and מרדכי are the same person. The name refers to his role as second to the king.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists מלאכי and מרדכי separately
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the prophets of the second year of דריוש and names מרדכי and מלאכי separately, so they seem to be two different people.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: ברוך son of נריה, שריה son of מחסיה, דניאל, מרדכי, בלשן, חגי, זכריה and מלאכי all prophesied in the second year of דריוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן with a ברייתא that lists מרדכי and מלאכי as two separate names in the same list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מלאכי were מרדכי, the ברייתא would not count him twice in one list. Naming them separately shows that the ברייתא saw them as two different prophets.

keyTerms.meaning: They prophesied
דריוש, the Persian king

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: בָּרוּךְ בֶּן נֵרִיָּה וּשְׂרָיָה בֶּן מַעֲשֵׂיָה,
phrases.english: Baruch son of Neriah, and Seraiah son of Mahseiah,
and Daniel, and Mordechai, Bilshan, and Haggai,
Zechariah and Malachi:
all of them prophesied in the second year of Darius.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's identification.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that מלאכי is מרדכי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists מרדכי and מלאכי as two separate names, so they must be two different people.

steps.title: רב נחמן is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא refutes רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that רב נחמן's view is refuted and offers no answer to save it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No answer is given for the ברייתא, so רב נחמן's identification is rejected. מלאכי and מרדכי are treated as two separate people.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation

steps.whatToRemember: Names in prophetic verses carry meaning: a named father was also a prophet (עולא), and named ancestors share the praise or blame (the ברייתא). רב נחמן's claim that מלאכי is מרדכי is refuted, because a ברייתא lists them separately.

phrases.english: It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes that the challenge in step 5 succeeds.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן's view is rejected. מלאכי is not מרדכי.

steps.title: A ברייתא debates whether מלאכי is עזרא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says מלאכי is really עזרא. The חכמים say מלאכי was the prophet's own name.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהושע בן קרחה said, 'מלאכי is עזרא.' The חכמים say, 'מלאכי was his real name.'
steps.whatsHappening: Right after rejecting רב נחמן's idea that מלאכי is מרדכי, the גמרא brings a ברייתא with a different suggestion: מלאכי is עזרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two opinions here. רבי יהושע בן קרחה says מלאכי was a second name for עזרא. The חכמים disagree and say מלאכי was a real, separate name, not a title for someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: The last of the prophets
עזרא the scribe, who led the return to ארץ ישראל
'מלאכי was his name.' It was his real name, not a nickname.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said:
Malachi is Ezra,
and the Sages say: Malachi was his name.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the idea that מלאכי is מרדכי was refuted, this step brings a new suggestion about who מלאכי was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Disagreement: רבי יהושע בן קרחה says מלאכי is עזרא; the חכמים say מלאכי is the prophet's real name.

steps.title: רב נחמן cites מלאכי's prophecy against intermarriage
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says it makes sense that מלאכי is עזרא. He points to a verse in מלאכי that criticizes Jews for marrying foreign women.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: It makes sense to follow the one who said מלאכי is עזרא. In מלאכי's prophecy it is written: 'יהודה has betrayed, and a disgusting thing was done in ישראל and in ירושלים, for יהודה made holy things profane, which ה׳ loves, and married the daughter of a foreign god.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן begins a proof for רבי יהושע בן קרחה. This step is the first half: it shows that מלאכי spoke out against marrying non-Jewish women. The next step will connect this to עזרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse shows that intermarriage was a main issue in מלאכי's prophecy. On its own this proves nothing yet. The proof needs a second piece showing who actually dealt with that same problem.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense; it is reasonable
Like the one who said (siding with an opinion)
The daughter of a foreign god, meaning a non-Jewish woman

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
It is reasonable to follow the one who said
Malachi is Ezra,
for it is written in the prophecy of Malachi:
"Judah has dealt treacherously,
and an abomination was done in Israel and in Jerusalem;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי חִלֵּל יְהוּדָה קֹדֶשׁ ה׳ אֲשֶׁר אָהֵב
phrases.english: for Judah profaned the holiness of the Lord, which He loves,
and married the daughter of a foreign god."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מִסְתַּבְּרָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר מַלְאָכִי זֶה עֶזְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יהושע בן קרחה's opinion from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that מלאכי is עזרא
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלאכי 2:11, which condemns marriage to foreign women

steps.title: עזרא is the one who sent away the foreign wives
steps.stepSummary: The proof is completed: עזרא is the leader who removed the non-Jewish wives, as a verse in ספר עזרא shows. So מלאכי and עזרא fought the same battle.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who separated the Jews from their non-Jewish wives? עזרא. As it is written: 'שכניה son of יחיאל, of the children of עילם, answered and said to עזרא: We have betrayed our God and married foreign women.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב נחמן's proof. It shows that עזרא was the leader who fought intermarriage, the same issue מלאכי prophesied about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלאכי condemned intermarriage, and עזרא is the one who acted to end it. Because both deal with the same problem at the same time, it makes sense that they are one person. This is a reasonable argument (מסתברא), not a strict proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Separated; removed
Foreign (non-Jewish) women
We betrayed; we acted unfaithfully

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן supports 'מלאכי is עזרא' because both מלאכי's prophecy and עזרא's actions focus on ending intermarriage.

phrases.english: And who removed the non-Jewish women? Ezra,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיַּעַן שְׁכַנְיָה בֶן יְחִיאֵל מִבְּנֵי עֵילָם
phrases.english: as it is written: "And Shecaniah son of Jehiel, of the sons of Elam, answered
and said to Ezra:
We have broken faith with our God
and have married foreign women."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 8 by linking the theme of the verse to עזרא.
steps.raayaObject: The opinion that מלאכי is עזרא
steps.raayaSupportSource: עזרא 10:2, where the people confess to עזרא that they married foreign women

steps.title: The four most beautiful women in the world
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists four women of great beauty: שרה, אביגיל, רחב, and אסתר. According to the view that אסתר was greenish in color, ושתי replaces her on the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There were four very beautiful women in the world: שרה, אביגיל, רחב, and אסתר. According to the one who says אסתר was greenish, take out אסתר and put in ושתי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new topic in אגדה about famous women, some of whom were among the prophetesses discussed earlier. A ברייתא lists the four most beautiful women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list has four names. There is a view elsewhere that אסתר was not naturally beautiful (she was 'greenish') and only had a special grace from ה׳. By that view, ושתי takes her place on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Very beautiful
Greenish, sallow in color
Take out and put in (swap one item for another)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
There were four exceptionally beautiful women in the world:
Sarah, Abigail, Rahab, and Esther.
And according to the one who says Esther was greenish,
remove Esther and insert Vashti.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַרְבַּע נָשִׁים יְפֵיפִיּוֹת הָיוּ בָּעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question of מלאכי and begins a new section of אגדה about famous women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four most beautiful women were שרה, אביגיל, רחב, and אסתר, with ושתי replacing אסתר according to the view that אסתר was greenish.

steps.title: How each of four women drew attention
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that רחב drew attention through her name, יעל through her voice, אביגיל through the memory of her, and מיכל בת שאול through her appearance.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: רחב caused desire through her name, יעל through her voice, אביגיל through being remembered, and מיכל the daughter of שאול through being seen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about these famous women. It explains what feature of each one caused men to be drawn to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each woman is matched with one feature: name, voice, memory, or sight. The point is how powerful their attractiveness was. For רחב, even hearing her name was enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: caused impure thoughts or desire
Through her voice
Through being remembered
Through being seen

steps.confusionAlert: זִינְּתָה here does not mean these women sinned. It means that this feature caused others to have impure thoughts about them.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Rahab aroused desire through her name;
Yael, through her voice;
Abigail, through the memory of her;
Michal, daughter of Saul, through her appearance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of famous beautiful women from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רחב drew desire by her name, יעל by her voice, אביגיל by memory, and מיכל by sight.

steps.title: רבי יצחק on the power of רחב's name
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says that anyone who says 'רחב, רחב' immediately becomes impure with קרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Anyone who says 'רחב, רחב' immediately has a seminal emission.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק adds a strong statement that builds on the ברייתא's claim that רחב drew desire through her name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said רחב's name alone stirred desire. רבי יצחק takes this further: just saying her name twice brings immediate physical arousal. This bold claim sets up רב נחמן's challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes impure through קרי (a seminal emission)
Immediately

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Anyone who says "Rahab, Rahab" immediately experiences an emission.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר רָחָב רָחָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the ברייתא's statement that רחב drew desire through her name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying רחב's name twice immediately causes קרי.

steps.title: רב נחמן says the name does not affect him
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges רבי יצחק from his own experience: he says 'רחב, רחב' and nothing happens to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: I say 'רחב, רחב' and it does not affect me!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges רבי יצחק's statement with a real-life test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק said 'anyone' (כל האומר) who says the name is affected. רב נחמן is proof that this is not true for everyone. So the statement as worded cannot be fully correct.

keyTerms.meaning: I say
It does not bother me; it has no effect on me

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to him:
I say "Rahab, Rahab"
and it does not affect me!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן: אֲנָא אָמֵינָא רָחָב רָחָב וְלָא אִיכְפַּת לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges רבי יצחק's statement in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's claim that anyone who says 'רחב, רחב' is affected
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counterexample: רב נחמן says the name and is not affected, so the claim cannot apply to everyone.

steps.title: רבי יצחק meant only someone who knew רחב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that his statement applies only to someone who knew רחב personally and recognized her.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When I said this, I meant someone who knows her and recognizes her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers רב נחמן by narrowing his statement. It was never meant for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'anyone' was too broad. It really means only a person who knew רחב and saw her beauty. רב נחמן never knew her, so he is not affected, and there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: When I said it, I meant
About one who knows her and recognizes her

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יצחק's statement about רחב's name applies only to someone who knew her personally. That is why רב נחמן was not affected.

phrases.english: He said to him:
When I said it, I meant one who knows her and recognizes her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כִּי קָאָמֵינָא בְּיוֹדְעָהּ וּבְמַכִּירָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב נחמן's challenge from step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the original statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן understood 'anyone' to mean every person who says the name.
steps.terutzMaskana: The statement applies only to one who knew רחב personally and recognized her beauty.

steps.title: What did מרדכי cry out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the מגילה. It quotes the verse about מרדכי learning of the decree and asks what words he actually cried out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And מרדכי knew all that had been done' (and he cried out loudly and bitterly). What did he say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to explaining the verses of the מגילה and asks a question. The next step will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says מרדכי cried out with a loud and bitter cry, but it never says what words he used. The גמרא wants to fill in that missing content.

keyTerms.meaning: מרדכי, the Jewish leader in the מגילה
was done (here, המן's decree)
What did he say?

steps.confusionAlert: This is a new topic. The discussion of רחב and the beautiful women is over, and the גמרא is now explaining פסוקים in the מגילה again.

phrases.english: "And Mordecai knew
all that had been done."
phrases.notes: אסתר ד:א. The verse goes on to say he cried out loudly and bitterly.

phrases.english: What did he say?
phrases.notes: What were the actual words he cried out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic about רחב and returns to explaining the verses of the מגילה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual words of מרדכי's bitter cry.

steps.title: רב and שמואל explain מרדכי's cry
steps.stepSummary: רב says מרדכי cried that המן had become greater than אחשורוש. שמואל says he cried, in softened language, that the 'upper King' had beaten the 'lower king'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: 'המן has risen higher than אחשורוש.' שמואל said: 'The upper King has won over the lower king.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question by each giving a version of what מרדכי cried out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, מרדכי cried that המן now controlled the empire even more than the king did. שמואל's words sound like 'God beat אחשורוש.' However, he is speaking politely and saying the reverse of what he means. He really means that it looks as if the lower king, אחשורוש, has beaten the upper King, הקב״ה.

keyTerms.meaning: rose higher, became greater
the upper King, meaning הקב״ה
the lower king, meaning אחשורוש

steps.confusionAlert: Read שמואל backwards. He is not saying God won. He uses a polite reversal so he does not have to say outright that a human king beat God.

phrases.english: Rav said: Haman has risen higher than Ahasuerus,
and Shmuel said:
The upper King has prevailed over the lower king.
phrases.notes: He says it backwards out of respect; he really means the lower king seems to have beaten the upper King.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב: המן became greater than אחשורוש. שמואל: in softened words, it seemed that אחשורוש had beaten הקב״ה.

steps.title: What does 'וַתִּתְחַלְחַל' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the verse saying the queen was badly shaken and asks what this unusual word means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And the queen was greatly shaken (וַתִּתְחַלְחַל).' What does 'וַתִּתְחַלְחַל' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next verse and asks about an unusual word. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word is a strong, doubled form, so the גמרא assumes it describes more than ordinary fear. It hints at the word חלל, meaning a hollow or opening in the body.

keyTerms.meaning: and she was deeply shaken (linked to חָלָל, a bodily cavity)
the queen (אסתר)

phrases.english: "And the queen was greatly shaken."
phrases.notes: אסתר ד:ד

phrases.english: What is "vatitchalchal"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next verse in the same section of the מגילה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the unusual word וַתִּתְחַלְחַל.

steps.title: אסתר's fear caused a physical reaction
steps.stepSummary: רב says אסתר became a נדה from fright. רבי ירמיה says her fear made her need to relieve herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: she began to menstruate. רבי ירמיה said: she needed to relieve herself.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים explain the word. Both say אסתר's fear was so great that her body reacted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both read 'וַתִּתְחַלְחַל' as coming from חלל, a bodily opening. They disagree only about which physical reaction the word describes.

keyTerms.meaning: began menstruating, became a נדה
her bodily openings (here, needing to relieve herself)

phrases.english: Rav said: That she began to menstruate,
and Rabbi Yirmeya said:
That she needed to relieve herself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Her terror caused a bodily reaction: becoming a נדה (רב) or loosened bowels (רבי ירמיה).

steps.title: התך was really דניאל
steps.stepSummary: רב identifies התך as דניאל. רב and שמואל each explain the name התך as coming from 'cut', but in opposite directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And אסתר called for התך.' רב said: התך is דניאל. Why was he called התך? Because he was 'cut down' from his high position. שמואל said: because all the kingdom's matters were 'cut', meaning decided, by his word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that the servant התך is really the נביא דניאל. It then explains why he had that name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both explanations come from the root חתך, 'to cut'. For רב, the name means he was cut down: once a great minister, he had been demoted to serving the queen. For שמואל, the name means the opposite: he was so important that every royal decision was 'cut', or finalized, by him.

keyTerms.meaning: התך, the queen's servant in the מגילה
דניאל the prophet
they cut him down from his greatness
were decided by his word

phrases.english: "And Esther called for Hathach,"
phrases.notes: אסתר ד:ה

phrases.english: Rav said: Hathach is Daniel,
and why was he called Hathach?
Because they cut him down from his greatness.
And Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁכׇּל דִּבְרֵי מַלְכוּת נֶחְתָּכִין עַל פִּיו.
phrases.english: Because all matters of the kingdom were decided by his word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues to the next verse in the same section of the מגילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: התך is דניאל. The name means either that he was demoted (רב) or that he decided all royal matters (שמואל).

steps.title: אסתר asks whether the Jews broke the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that 'מה זה ועל מה זה' was אסתר asking whether the Jews had sinned against the Torah. He links the word 'זה' to the לוחות, which were written 'מזה ומזה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'To know what this is and why this is.' רבי יצחק said: she sent to him, 'Perhaps the Jews have sinned against the five books of the Torah,' since it is written about the לוחות: 'On this side and on that side they were written.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains what אסתר was really asking מרדכי when she sent התך to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse uses the word 'זה' twice. רבי יצחק connects it to the לוחות, which were written 'מזה ומזה', on both sides. So 'זה' hints at the Torah. אסתר assumed a decree this terrible must come from a sin, and she asked whether the Jews had abandoned the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: what is this and why is this
she sent a message to him
the five books of the Torah
on this side and on that side (said of the לוחות)

steps.whatToRemember: In this section, each unusual word in מגילת אסתר chapter 4 opens a deeper meaning: מרדכי's cry, אסתר's fright, the identity of התך as דניאל, and אסתר's worry that the decree came because of sin against the Torah.

phrases.english: "To know what this is, and why this is."
phrases.notes: אסתר ד:ה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said: She sent to him:
Perhaps the Jews have transgressed
the five books of the Torah,
as it is written about them:
"On this side and on that side they were written."
phrases.notes: שמות לב:טו, about the לוחות. The shared word 'זה' links the two verses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same verse: having said who התך was, it now explains the message אסתר sent with him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אסתר asked whether the decree came because the Jews had transgressed the Torah, which is hinted at by the word 'זה' from the לוחות.

steps.title: התך did not bring back the bad news himself
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'they' told מרדכי, not התך himself. From this the גמרא learns that a person should not be the one to deliver a bad report.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And they told מרדכי אסתר's words.' But התך himself did not go to him. From here we learn that one does not bring back a bad report.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the פסוק switches to 'they told' instead of naming התך, and learns a lesson in proper behavior from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now התך was the messenger between אסתר and מרדכי. Now that אסתר's answer was discouraging ('I can't go to the king'), the פסוק says 'they' told him, meaning other messengers. This shows that a person should avoid being the one who delivers bad news.

keyTerms.meaning: And they told (plural, meaning not התך alone)
Whereas he himself
To him
One does not bring back a bad or sad report

phrases.english: "And they told Mordecai the words of Esther,"
phrases.notes: אסתר ד:יב. The key word is the plural 'they'.

phrases.english: whereas he (Hathach) himself did not go to him.
phrases.notes: Up to now התך carried every message.

phrases.english: From here we learn that one does not bring back a bad report.
phrases.notes: The answer אסתר sent was discouraging, so התך let others carry it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the running commentary on מגילת אסתר chapter 4, building on step 19's identification of התך as the messenger.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not be the bearer of bad news. This is learned from the plural 'ויגידו'.

steps.title: אסתר goes to the king willingly for the first time
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא explains 'אשר לא כדת' to mean that, unlike every other time, אסתר would now go to אחשורוש willingly and not by force.
steps.simpleTranslation: אסתר said: 'Go, gather all the Jews…' until 'which is not according to the custom.' רבי אבא said: It was not like the usual way. Every day until now it was against my will, and now it is by my own choice.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא explains the phrase 'not according to the custom' in אסתר's message to מרדכי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple reading is that going to the king without being called breaks palace rules. רבי אבא adds a deeper layer: it was also 'not like usual' for אסתר personally. Until now she was with אחשורוש only by force, but this time she was choosing to go to him herself.

keyTerms.meaning: Gather
According to the custom or law
By force, against one's will
Willingly, by choice

phrases.english: "Go, gather all the Jews" etc.
phrases.notes: אסתר ד:טז

phrases.english: until "which is not according to the custom,"
phrases.notes: This is the phrase being explained.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
It was not according to the usual way,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבְּכׇל יוֹם וָיוֹם עַד עַכְשָׁיו — בְּאוֹנֶס,
phrases.english: for every single day until now, it was by force,
but now, it is willingly.
phrases.notes: She chose to go to אחשורוש herself in order to save the Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: שֶׁלֹּא כַּדָּת הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק, אסתר's reply to מרדכי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לא כדת' means that for the first time אסתר would go to אחשורוש willingly rather than by force.

steps.title: אסתר will now be lost to מרדכי
steps.stepSummary: The double word 'אבדתי אבדתי' is read as two losses. אסתר was already lost to her father's house, and now she will also be lost to מרדכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And if I perish, I perish.' Just as I was lost from my father's house, so I will be lost from you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the פסוק says 'perish' twice. It continues the idea from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first 'אבדתי' is the loss of being taken from her family to the palace. The second is a new loss: because she would now go to אחשורוש willingly, she would become forbidden to מרדכי (her husband, according to חז"ל) forever. So this step is the result of רבי אבא's point that this time it was 'ברצון'.

keyTerms.meaning: I am lost, I perish
My father's house, my family
I will be lost from you

steps.confusionAlert: 'Lost to you' does not mean she expected to die. It means that by going willingly to אחשורוש she would become forbidden to מרדכי, who חז"ל say was her husband.

phrases.english: "And if I perish, I perish":
phrases.notes: The double wording points to two losses.

phrases.english: just as I was lost from my father's house,
so I will be lost from you.
phrases.notes: Going willingly would make her forbidden to מרדכי.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאָבַדְתִּי מִבֵּית אַבָּא, כָּךְ אוֹבַד מִמְּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds directly on step 22. Because she was now going willingly, she would be lost to מרדכי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The double 'אבדתי' means two losses: she was lost to her family, and now she would be lost to מרדכי.

steps.title: What it means that מרדכי 'passed'
steps.stepSummary: רב says מרדכי made the first day of פסח a fast day. שמואל says he crossed over a stream of water.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And מרדכי passed.' רב said: He passed the first day of פסח in a fast. שמואל said: He crossed a stream of water.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל disagree about what the word 'ויעבור' means in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב connects 'ויעבור' to 'עבירה', a transgression. מרדכי fasted on the first day of פסח, which normally is a day of rejoicing, because the three-day fast started on the 14th of ניסן. שמואל reads it simply as 'crossed over': מרדכי crossed a stream to gather the Jews.

keyTerms.meaning: And he passed or crossed
He passed (a day) or let go by
A fast
A stream or channel of water

steps.whyThisMatters: רב's reading shows that saving Jewish lives was important enough for מרדכי to set aside the מצוה of rejoicing on יום טוב.

phrases.english: "And Mordecai passed."
phrases.notes: אסתר ד:יז

phrases.english: Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֶעֱבִיר יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח בְּתַעֲנִית.
phrases.english: that he passed the first day of Pesach in a fast.
phrases.notes: Related to the word עבירה (transgression), since the day should be one of joy.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
that he crossed a stream of water.
phrases.notes: The plain meaning of 'crossing'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: שֶׁהֶעֱבִיר יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל פֶּסַח בְּתַעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next פסוק. מרדכי carries out אסתר's request to gather the Jews and fast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב says 'ויעבור' means he fasted on the first day of פסח. שמואל says it means he crossed a stream.

steps.title: Why does the verse say she wore 'royalty' and not 'royal clothes'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a problem in the wording. A person wears royal clothes, not 'royalty' itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And it was on the third day, and אסתר wore royalty.' It should have said 'royal clothes'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a difficulty with the wording of the פסוק. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logically, a person puts on clothing, so the פסוק should have said 'בגדי מלכות'. The missing word 'clothes' suggests the פסוק is hinting at something beyond physical clothing.

keyTerms.meaning: And she wore or clothed herself
Royalty, kingship
Royal clothes
It should have said

phrases.english: "And it was on the third day,
phrases.notes: אסתר ה:א, the third day of the fast.

phrases.english: and Esther wore royalty."
It should have said "royal clothes"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק (chapter 5) and challenges its wording.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: You wear clothing, not 'royalty', so the פסוק seems to be missing the word 'בגדי'.

steps.title: אסתר was clothed in רוח הקודש
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי חנינא, explains that 'מלכות' here means רוח הקודש. He proves it from the same word 'clothing' used for עמשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא: This teaches that רוח הקודש clothed her. It is written here 'and she wore', and it is written there 'and the spirit clothed עמשי'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 25. The 'royalty' אסתר wore was רוח הקודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer uses a word comparison. The verb 'לבש' (to clothe) appears both here and in דברי הימים, where a spirit 'clothed' עמשי. Just as there it means a spirit from ה׳, here too 'royalty' means a spiritual garment, רוח הקודש. That explains why the פסוק does not say 'clothes'.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches
Divine inspiration
It is written here, and it is written there (a comparison of words)
עמשי, a leader in the time of דוד

steps.whatToRemember: אסתר's 'royalty' was spiritual. On the third day of the fast she was clothed in רוח הקודש before going to the king.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
This teaches that Divine inspiration clothed her.
It is written here: "and she wore,"
and it is written there: "and the spirit clothed Amasai."
phrases.notes: דברי הימים א יב:יט. The same verb 'clothe' is used for a spirit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording difficulty raised in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the word through a verbal comparison (לבש / לבשה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מלכות' would mean physical royal garments, but then the word 'בגדי' is missing.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מלכות' refers to רוח הקודש, which 'clothed' her, just as a spirit clothed עמשי.

steps.title: Do not take lightly the blessing of an ordinary person
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי חנינא, teaches that a blessing from a הדיוט should never seem small to you. Two great people of their generation were blessed by ordinary people, and those blessings came true.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא: Never let the blessing of an ordinary person seem small in your eyes. Two of the greatest men of their generations were blessed by two ordinary people, and the blessings came true for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from the same pair, רבי אלעזר quoting רבי חנינא, who were quoted in the previous step. This one teaches that a simple person's blessing has real power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This topic is new and is not connected to the מגילה story. The גמרא brings it only because it comes from the same speakers. The proof is given in general terms here: 'two great men'. The next step names who they were.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary, simple person, not a great scholar or leader
The blessing of an ordinary person
Light (unimportant) in your eyes
The great people of the generation
It was fulfilled; it came true

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a continuation of the explanation of 'ותלבש אסתר מלכות'. The גמרא is simply collecting more teachings from רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי חנינא, because a teaching of theirs was just quoted.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Ḥanina said:
phrases.notes: Same chain of speakers as Step 26, which is why this teaching is brought here.

phrases.english: Never let the blessing of an ordinary person be
light in your eyes,
for two of the great men of the generation
were blessed by two ordinary people,
and it was fulfilled in them,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לְעוֹלָם אַל תְּהִי בִּרְכַּת הֶדְיוֹט קַלָּה בְּעֵינֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Associative link: this is another teaching from the same speakers as Step 26. The topic is new.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Never take lightly the blessing of an ordinary person, because such blessings can come true.

steps.title: The examples of דוד and דניאל
steps.stepSummary: The two great men were דוד, who was blessed by ארונה, and דניאל, who was blessed by the king דריוש. Both blessings came true.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are דוד and דניאל. דוד was blessed by ארונה, as it says: 'And ארונה said to the king, may ה׳ your God accept you.' דניאל was blessed by דריוש, as it says: 'Your God, Whom you serve constantly, He will save you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the two great men from the previous step. It brings a פסוק for each one to show the blessing they received.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ארונה was an ordinary person, and his blessing that ה׳ would accept דוד came true. דריוש was a non-Jewish king, not a spiritual figure, yet his blessing came true when דניאל was saved from the lions' den. Both examples show that even a simple or unexpected source of a blessing should be taken seriously.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jebusite who sold דוד the place of the future בית המקדש and blessed him
דריוש, the king who threw דניאל into the lions' den
Constantly, always (Aramaic)
He will save you (Aramaic)

steps.whatToRemember: A blessing from anyone, even a simple person or a non-Jewish king, can come true. דוד and דניאל are the proof.

phrases.english: And these are they: David and Daniel.
David, whom Araunah blessed,
as it is written: “And Araunah said to the king, etc.”
phrases.notes: The verse continues: 'May ה׳ your God accept you' (שמואל ב כד:כג).

phrases.english: Daniel, whom Darius blessed,
as it is written: “Your God Whom you serve
continually, He will save you.”
phrases.notes: This came true when דניאל was saved from the lions' den (דניאל ו:יז).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the two great men and brings פסוקים to prove the claim made in Step 27.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the blessing of a הדיוט can be fulfilled
steps.raayaSupportSource: The blessing of ארונה to דוד (שמואל ב כד:כג) and of דריוש to דניאל (דניאל ו:יז)

steps.title: Do not take lightly the curse of an ordinary person
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי חנינא, teaches that an ordinary person's curse can also come true. אבימלך said to שרה 'a covering of the eyes', and this came true when her son יצחק became blind.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא: Do not let the curse of an ordinary person seem small in your eyes. אבימלך cursed שרה, saying 'It is for you a covering of the eyes', and it came true in her child: 'And when יצחק was old, his eyes became dim.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second teaching from the same speakers, and it is the mirror image of the first. Just as a simple person's blessing can come true, so can a simple person's curse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבימלך's phrase 'כסות עינים' (a covering of the eyes) is read as an unintended curse on שרה. It was fulfilled in her son יצחק, whose eyes later became dim. The link is the shared idea of the eyes being covered.

keyTerms.meaning: The curse of an ordinary person
The king of גרר who took שרה
A covering of the eyes
In her descendant (here, her son יצחק)
And they became dim

steps.confusionAlert: In the פסוק, אבימלך's words do not sound like a curse at all. The גמרא reads them as a hidden curse because of how they later came true in יצחק's eyes.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Ḥanina said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵל תְּהִי קִלְלַת הֶדְיוֹט קַלָּה בְּעֵינֶיךָ,
phrases.english: Do not let the curse of an ordinary person be light in your eyes,
for Abimelech cursed Sarah:
“Behold, it is for you a covering of the eyes,”
phrases.notes: בראשית כ:טז

phrases.english: and it was fulfilled in her offspring:
“And it came to pass, when Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim.”
phrases.notes: בראשית כז:א

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: אֵל תְּהִי קִלְלַת הֶדְיוֹט קַלָּה בְּעֵינֶיךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching: Step 27 was about blessings, and this step is about curses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Never take lightly the curse of an ordinary person, because it can come true, as happened to יצחק.

steps.title: ה׳ puts in the water before the pot
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי חנינא, contrasts people with הקדוש ברוך הוא. A person puts the pot on the fire first and then adds water. ה׳ first put the water in place and then made the 'pot', the heavens, to hold it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא: Come and see that ה׳'s way is not like the way of people. People put a pot on the fire and then put water into it. But ה׳ puts in the water first and then puts the pot on the fire, as the פסוק says: 'At the sound of His giving a mass of water in the heavens.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third teaching from the same speakers. It compares how people work with how ה׳ created the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person cannot pour water into a pot that does not exist yet. ה׳ is not limited this way: He set the waters in place first and then formed the heavens around them. The פסוק is read as 'He gave the waters, and then the heavens'.

keyTerms.meaning: The way of a human being (literally, 'flesh and blood')
Places a pot on the fire
The Holy One, Blessed be He (ה׳)
Come and see, an opening for a lesson

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Ḥanina said:

phrases.aramaic: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: Come and see that unlike the attribute of the Holy One, Blessed be He,
is the attribute of flesh and blood.

phrases.aramaic: מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וָדָם — אָדָם שׁוֹפֵת קְדֵרָה
phrases.english: The way of flesh and blood: a person places a pot on the fire
and afterward puts water into it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא — נוֹתֵן מַיִם
phrases.english: but the Holy One, Blessed be He, puts in the water
and afterward places the pot on the fire,
to fulfill that which is stated:
“At the sound of His giving a multitude of waters in the heavens.”
phrases.notes: ירמיה י:יג. The waters were given first, and then the heavens were formed to hold them.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֹּא וּרְאֵה שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִדַּת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִדַּת בָּשָׂר וְדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching in the same string. The topic is new: how ה׳'s creation differs from human actions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ placed the waters first and then made the heavens to hold them, the reverse of how a person cooks.

steps.title: Quoting someone by name brings redemption
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי חנינא, teaches that whoever repeats something in the name of the person who said it brings גאולה to the world. The proof is that אסתר told the king about the plot in the name of מרדכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא: Anyone who says something in the name of the person who said it brings redemption to the world, as it says: 'And אסתר told the king in the name of מרדכי.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is another teaching in the string from רבי אלעזר quoting רבי חנינא. Its proof brings us back to the מגילה story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אסתר reported the plot of בגתן ותרש and gave credit to מרדכי. Because of this, מרדכי's good deed was written down. Later the king rewarded him, which started the chain of events that saved the Jews. Giving proper credit led directly to the גאולה of פורים.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of the one who said it
Redemption; salvation
Brings

steps.whatToRemember: Giving credit to the one who said something brings גאולה. We learn this from אסתר, who reported the plot in מרדכי's name, which set up the miracle of פורים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous and practical lesson for learning and teaching Torah: always say a teaching in the name of the person who said it.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Whoever says a matter in the name of the one who said it
brings redemption to the world,
as it is stated: “And Esther told the king in the name of Mordecai.”
phrases.notes: אסתר ב:כב, about the plot of בגתן ותרש.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר דָּבָר בְּשֵׁם אוֹמְרוֹ מֵבִיא גְּאוּלָּה לָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching in the string from רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי חנינא. Its proof ties back to the מגילה. More teachings from the same pair follow in steps 32–33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying a teaching in the name of the one who said it brings גאולה, as shown by אסתר crediting מרדכי.

steps.title: When a righteous man dies, the loss belongs to his generation
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי חנינא, teaches that when a צדיק is 'lost' (dies), only his generation loses. The parable is a lost pearl, which is still a pearl wherever it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא: When a righteous man is lost, he is lost only to his generation. This is like a man who lost a pearl. Wherever the pearl is, it is still called a pearl. It is lost only to its owner.
steps.whatsHappening: This is another teaching in the chain from רבי אלעזר quoting רבי חנינא. It says that when a צדיק passes away, the real loss belongs to the people left behind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדיק himself loses nothing, because he stays a צדיק wherever he goes, like a pearl that keeps its value. The people of his generation are the ones who lose, because they no longer have him among them. The parable makes the abstract idea concrete: the owner suffers the loss, not the pearl.

keyTerms.meaning: A righteous person
Was lost (here, a gentle way of saying 'died')
To his generation
A parable or comparison
A pearl or precious gem
Its owner

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching explains why we mourn a צדיק. We are not mourning for him, since he has lost nothing. We are mourning for ourselves, because we lost his presence.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Chanina said:
phrases.notes: The same pair of names continues from the earlier steps.

phrases.english: A righteous man who is lost is lost to his generation.
phrases.notes: The word 'lost' refers to his passing away.

phrases.english: It is like a man who lost a pearl,
wherever it is, it is still called a pearl,
phrases.notes: The pearl keeps its value no matter where it ends up.

phrases.english: it is lost only to its owner.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is another separate teaching in the series from רבי אלעזר quoting רבי חנינא. It continues the list from steps 27-31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The death of a צדיק is a loss to his generation, not to himself, just as a lost pearl is a loss only to its owner.

steps.title: המן said 'all this is worth nothing' when he saw מרדכי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes המן's words 'all this is worth nothing to me.' רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי חנינא, explains that המן said this at the moment he saw מרדכי sitting at the king's gate.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Yet all this is worth nothing to me.' רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי חנינא: When המן saw מרדכי sitting at the king's gate, he said, 'All this is worth nothing to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from מגילת אסתר. Then רבי אלעזר, quoting רבי חנינא, explains when and why המן said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: המן had wealth, children, and honor, so it is strange that he says none of it is worth anything. The teaching ties his frustration to one specific sight: מרדכי sitting at the king's gate. This opens a question the גמרא answers next: why did that particular sight bother him so much?

keyTerms.meaning: It is not worth anything to me
המן, the villain of the מגילה
מרדכי, the hero of the מגילה
The king's gate, a place of royal officials

phrases.english: "Yet all this is worth nothing to me" (Esther 5:13).
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק being explained.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Chanina said:
At the time that Haman saw
Mordechai sitting at the king's gate,
he said: "All this is worth nothing to me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a new teaching in the same series. This time it explains a פסוק in the מגילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: המן's statement that all his success was worthless was triggered by seeing מרדכי sitting at the king's gate.

steps.title: רב חסדא explains why seeing מרדכי upset המן so much
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רב חסדא to explain המן's frustration. רב חסדא contrasts the two men: מרדכי came as a wealthy, high-status person, and המן came in a lower position. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: This fits the teaching of רב חסדא, for רב חסדא said: This one (מרדכי) came as a wealthy man, and that one (המן) came…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רב חסדא to explain why seeing מרדכי ruined everything for המן. The amud ends in the middle of רב חסדא's sentence, so the explanation finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא compares the status of the two men. מרדכי is described as coming 'בפרוזבולי', meaning as someone of wealth and standing. The second half of the contrast, describing המן's lower status, has not appeared yet, so we must wait for the next passage to see the full reason for המן's bitterness.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with the teaching of רב חסדא
As a wealthy person (a man of assets and standing)
This one... and that one (a contrast between two people)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse פרוזבולי here with the halachic פרוזבול that protects loans from שמיטה. Here the word describes a rich, high-status person. Also, the sentence is cut off: the description of המן comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: This is in line with Rav Chisda,
for Rav Chisda said:
This one (Mordechai) came as a wealthy man
phrases.notes: It refers to someone with assets and standing.

phrases.english: and that one (Haman) came…
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It explains step 33 by giving the reason why seeing מרדכי at the king's gate made המן feel his success was worthless.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב חסדא, מרדכי and המן came from contrasting levels of status, with מרדכי as the wealthy one. The full contrast continues on the next amud.
